title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
abstract: Introduces retrieval-augmented generation that combines a parametric sequence-to-sequence model with non-parametric retrieved passages, improving knowledge-intensive generation and enabling source-grounded outputs.

title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
abstract: Presents an approach that interleaves reasoning traces and environment actions, allowing language models to gather external information, update plans, and produce more interpretable task trajectories.

title: AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation
abstract: Describes a framework where customizable conversational agents cooperate through messages, tools, code execution, and human input to implement complex multi-agent workflows.

title: STORM: Assisting in Writing Wikipedia-like Articles From Scratch with Large Language Models
abstract: Studies automated knowledge curation for long-form report writing using retrieval, perspective-guided question asking, simulated conversations, outline construction, and citation-aware synthesis.

title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Introduces a feedback-driven agent architecture that stores verbal reflections after task attempts, using them as episodic memory to improve later planning and execution without parameter updates.

title: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
abstract: Explores iterative generation, self-feedback, and refinement using the same language model, showing that explicit critique-and-revision loops can improve outputs across diverse generation tasks.

title: SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering
abstract: Investigates how agent-computer interfaces and tool design affect language-model agents solving repository-level software tasks, emphasizing iterative observation, action, and environment feedback.

title: Corrective Retrieval Augmented Generation
abstract: Proposes a corrective retrieval-augmented generation strategy that evaluates retrieved evidence quality and triggers alternative retrieval or refinement when evidence is unreliable.
